comparison_scope: One bounded same-task comparison of the approved source first-component section with the larger homepage candidate document, plus contract inspection of whole-file digest and structural homepage tools. This is not a broad quality, reliability, or cost benchmark.
findings: The exact-copy task concerns one marker-delimited section inside a larger candidate file. The whole-file digest tools compare complete files and cannot show that the selected section matches when surrounding document content differs.
The homepage component validator checks declared component shape/count; it does not compare a section with caller-supplied authorized source text.

This tool checks one explicit section by exact UTF-8 bytes and reports hashes/offsets only. It does not fetch or authenticate the source, establish source approval, decide semantic equivalence, or authorize edits or publication.
The real task output matched the source section and candidate section at 2,403 bytes each. This demonstrates one narrow use case only; it does not establish broad reliability or analyst-time savings.
unique_remaining_use_cases: Compare one approved/caller-supplied source section with the corresponding section of a larger checked-out human document when whole-file equality is intentionally not expected.
Record exact selected-section byte identity and offsets without storing the compared text in the result.

estimated_cost.basis: No matched latency, resource, or analyst-time benchmark was run; one candidate file is capped at 2 MiB and source stdin at 512,000 bytes.

claim_ceiling: One repository-local exact-byte comparison for one caller-supplied source document and one checked-out candidate document. Source authenticity, authorship, approval, semantic equivalence, edit permission, release permission and scientific truth remain unestablished.
